title: Coordinates Lookup Tool: Map, Record and Facts
description: Look up a coordinate on a map and read available Nominatim address fields.
summary_sentence: Enter decimal latitude and longitude in separate fields or click the map to look up nearby mapped address information.
quick_answer: This workspace plots a selected point and requests available address fields from Nominatim. It does not calculate an antipode, equator distance or derived bearings.
steps_intro: Enter decimal coordinates, search a place or click the map:

body.t: Inspect available address fields for a coordinate from a log or photograph; the result is not a verified boundary.
Compare a point and a reverse-geocoded name for initial orientation. Check authoritative data for important decisions.
Use returned address fields as preliminary context, checking their source and date independently.
Use the related antipode and distance tools separately for calculations this lookup does not provide.
Enter latitude and longitude in the separate input fields, then press Look up to request address information.
A point in a sparsely mapped area may have few or no address fields. This does not prove a jurisdiction or feature is absent.

popular_table.title: What the lookup returns
popular_table.intro: Inputs and outputs for one selected point.
popular_table.note: Nominatim resolves a nearby suitable mapped object; the result is not guaranteed to describe the exact point.

faq: A map point and available reverse-geocoded address fields. It does not calculate antipodes or equator distance.
Can I click instead of typing?
Yes. Clicking the map looks up that point.
Enter decimal latitude and longitude in separate fields.
Returned address fields have copy controls; the coordinates are displayed on the page.
The selected coordinate is sent to Nominatim for reverse geocoding; a place search also uses an external geocoder. See the privacy page.
Can I look up a batch?
This workspace handles one point at a time.
